chapter: Le Ruban Bleu, retirement and community work
title: Free-lancing and deciding it was time to stop
summary: Probably theater engagements and Canadian clubs; as a commercial act she couldn't draw, so she retired.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: I got you. And inbetween what
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Oh, probably a theater engagement out west someplace, or a club somewhere. I don't know, a six-week tour or something on some theater circuit.
I probably went up to Canada, Toronto to clubs and things like that.
Okay, so you were just working on the road?

Yeah, well you see, as I said before I was free-lancing more or less so different agents if they had work, if they had a trio and they wanted a feature singer they'd call me. So I'd probably go some place for a two-week engagement in a club or wind up in some theater on a bill, you know, fill in. So I kept pretty busy up until 1957. I was tired in 1957. I really had it. I remember I wound up in Des Moines, Iowa, one leg of a long jump. I worked on a bill with Donny Donagan at a club there. And business wasn't that great so if you're - it looks like you're milking the business you're so - it's time to get out. You're on borrowed
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

time. So, it all led up to that because if you figure you can't draw, if you're a commercial artist and if you're being sold as such you expect it to draw. And if you're not drawing the crowd you begin to get dirty looks from the management, you know, so I've had it.
And that's how you thought of yourself, as a commercial?

Yeah, and I figured it was time to stop. And things weren't that great either in New York at the time because clubs were opening and closing like mad. And it wasn't that easy to get into an established club. In the meantime even the Ruban Bleu had closed. Herbert Jacoby opened the room, the Blue Angel, and then there was the up-town and the down-town cafe society. And another room that Herbert Jacoby opened was the (Direct Rod) and it stayed open four weeks. So things weren't too good. There might have been alot of little clubs that had been in forever. They weren't getting any pressure but the clubs that were really trying to make it weren't doing that well. I wasn't going to go out on the road. That's for sure. Especially doing one-nighters. That's rough.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Well, so you had gone through a rather lengthly period of things slowing down?

I had done very well, twenty years, you know. And in those days, I mean, you were supposed to retire. I think in those days people were retiring at age 45. That was supposed to be the retirement age. There was no law that said you had to retire at 45 but at 45 you were supposed to have, if you had been successful you've had it. It's time to quit. Now you can be successful till you're a hundred. Thank goodness for that.
